hints: Identify all three forces acting on particle $P$: tension $T_A$ at $20^\circ$ above the horizontal to the left, tension $T_B$ at $40^\circ$ above the horizontal to the right, and weight $W = mg = 1.6 \times 10 = 16\text{ N}$ acting vertically downwards.
Resolve forces horizontally to establish the first equilibrium equation: $T_A\cos 20^\circ = T_B\cos 40^\circ$.
Resolve forces vertically for the second equilibrium equation: $T_A\sin 20^\circ + T_B\sin 40^\circ = 16$.
Express $T_A$ in terms of $T_B$ as $T_A = T_B\frac{\cos 40^\circ}{\cos 20^\circ}$, substitute into the vertical equation, and solve for $T_B$, then evaluate $T_A$ to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
State the condition for a particle in coplanar equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \Sigma F_y = 0$$

Calculate the weight of the particle using $W = mg$ with mass $m = 1.6\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$W = 1.6 \times 10 = 16\text{ N}$$

Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation (taking right as positive):
$$T_B\cos 40^\circ - T_A\cos 20^\circ = 0 \implies T_A\cos 20^\circ = T_B\cos 40^\circ$$

Rearrange to express $T_A$ in terms of $T_B$ by dividing both sides by $\cos 20^\circ$:
$$T_A = T_B \times \frac{\cos 40^\circ}{\cos 20^\circ}$$

Set up the vertical equilibrium equation (taking upwards as positive):
$$T_A\sin 20^\circ + T_B\sin 40^\circ - 16 = 0 \implies T_A\sin 20^\circ + T_B\sin 40^\circ = 16$$

Substitute the expression for $T_A$ into the vertical equation:
$$\left(T_B \times \frac{\cos 40^\circ}{\cos 20^\circ}\right)\sin 20^\circ + T_B\sin 40^\circ = 16$$

Factor out $T_B$ on the left-hand side:
$$T_B\left(\cos 40^\circ \tan 20^\circ + \sin 40^\circ\right) = 16$$

Evaluate the trigonometric terms inside the brackets using standard values:
$$\cos 40^\circ \approx 0.766044, \quad \tan 20^\circ \approx 0.363970, \quad \sin 40^\circ \approx 0.642788$$
$$\cos 40^\circ \tan 20^\circ + \sin 40^\circ \approx (0.766044 \times 0.363970) + 0.642788 = 0.278817 + 0.642788 = 0.921605$$

Divide $16$ by $0.921605$ to find $T_B$:
$$T_B = \frac{16}{0.921605} \approx 17.3610\text{ N} = 17.4\text{ N} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$

Substitute $T_B = 17.3610\text{ N}$ back into the equation for $T_A$:
$$T_A = 17.3610 \times \frac{0.766044}{0.939693} = 17.3610 \times 0.815207 \approx 14.1528\text{ N} = 14.2\text{ N} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
